children: Arizona has filed a lawsuit against L’Oréal SA
and its US subsidiary, alleging the cosmetics company failed to disclose potential cancer risks associated with its hair-relaxer products.

Attorney General Kristin Mayes filed the case in state court Thursday, making Arizona the first state to pursue legal action over alleged cancer risks tied to hair relaxers. The state is seeking financial penalties and damages, along with an order requiring L’Oréal
to warn consumers about the alleged risks or stop selling the products.

The lawsuit focuses on hair relaxers sold under brands including Dark and Lovely and Optimum. The products, which permanently straighten textured hair, are used predominantly by African American women.
and related companies marketed the products to women and children for decades while failing to adequately address potential health concerns.
The lawsuit adds to more than 12,000 similar cases filed by women and their families, which have been consolidated in federal court in Chicago.
The litigation gained momentum after a 2022 National Institutes of Health study reported that women who frequently used hair relaxers were more than twice as likely to develop uterine cancer.
USA has rejected the allegations, saying its products are safe and that the claims lack scientific and legal merit.

title: L’Oréal faces Arizona suit over alleged hair relaxer cancer risks
